step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified system components from World Model and transcript: Satellite (ThirdParty), EC2 SPOT (EC2), S3 (S3), RDS (RDS), ELASTICACHE (ElastiCache), AWS FARGATE (Fargate), LAMBDA (Lambda), and User (UserConsumerWeb).
2. Assigned numeric node IDs sequentially from '0' to '7'.
3. Traced three main logical flows:
   - Flow 0: Ingestion pipeline where Satellite imagery is processed by EC2 Spot instances and stored into S3 (bulk data, ~5PB catalog, ~100GB/day) and RDS (metadata).
   - Flow 1: Web tile generation where User requests map tiles from Fargate, which checks ElastiCache, queries RDS metadata, fetches imagery chunks from S3 via HTTP range requests, writes tiles back to ElastiCache, and serves them to the user.
   - Flow 2: Time-series analysis where User sends custom field boundaries to Lambda, which queries RDS for metadata, pulls source imagery from S3, computes time-series greenness metrics, and returns the result to the user.
4. Mapped edges with flow_id, seq, type, and descriptive notes while ensuring valid vocabulary and node fields.

graph.name: Indigo Carbon Satellite Imagery Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture for processing daily satellite imagery from NASA to calculate carbon credit metrics and field health time-series data for farmers.

nodes.name: Satellite
nodes.notes: External satellite imagery source providing daily corrected tiles.

nodes.name: EC2 SPOT
nodes.notes: Auto-scaling cluster of EC2 Spot instances that post-process raw satellite tiles.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Bulk storage holding ~5 PB of imagery data spanning 10-30 years, growing ~100 GB/day.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Relational database storing imagery metadata and tile spatial references.

nodes.name: AWS FARGATE
nodes.notes: Fargate container service generating web map tiles on-the-fly using HTTP range requests.

nodes.name: ELASTICACHE
nodes.notes: Redis cache in ElastiCache storing pre-rendered common map tiles.

nodes.name: LAMBDA
nodes.notes: Series of Lambda functions performing custom field time-series calculations.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: Farmers and users interacting with the web application.
